goal: Execute the already-frozen label-independent, structurally counterbalanced native Qwen3-0.6B discriminator and distinguish internal representational transport from behavioral semantic vector control.

resolved_wrapper_failures: old GGUF and llama.cpp cache paths did not match the native cache namespace
pgrep-based liveness checks self-matched the wrapper command line
llama-ext.h required the pinned llama.cpp src include path
native shared libraries are in the split build directory rather than llama.cpp/build/bin

observed: The native cvec intervention produces strong sign-sensitive target-coordinate transport at the downstream nonterminal layer.
The same matched intervention does not improve target-code behavior; mean matched margin delta is negative and hit rate remains chance-level 1/3.
The class-selective behavioral causal matrix has a negative diagonal advantage.
The nuisance control causes a larger mean absolute behavioral delta than the matched semantic intervention.
Calibration and holdout use lexically disjoint content symbols and opaque A/B/C code identity is counterbalanced across all semantic targets.
inference: The tested residualized internal direction is a transported representation but is not established as a sufficient behavioral semantic actuator under native ALL_PROMPT_TOKENS cvec broadcast.
This result is counterevidence against treating the earlier last-token witness and native broadcast cvec as causally identical interventions.
A strong internal coordinate displacement cannot by itself justify semantic J-Space promotion.
not_established: The result does not prove that no alternative layer, scope, vector orientation, subspace, or actuator can provide abstract semantic control.
method_quality_notes: The semantic simplex is centered before nuisance projection, so common activation offset is not used as semantic geometry.

The current discriminator holdout is small (9 cases) and its PASS rule is inequality-based rather than confidence/permutation-test based; therefore even a hypothetical PASS would remain bounded component evidence.

The all-prompt-token native broadcast can perturb demonstration/codebook processing as well as the probe state, so scope-localization remains a key next discriminator rather than a solved equivalence.
next_exact_discriminator: Do not retune on the opened holdout. On a fresh preregistered family split, compare the same residualized semantic subspace under scope-localized native intervention (probe-boundary/late-token or other API-equivalent localization if technically available) versus ALL_PROMPT_TOKENS broadcast, with sign orientation frozen on calibration, full semantic-target x code-identity counterbalance, nuisance-matched controls, downstream transport, emitted-decision readout, and permutation/bootstrap uncertainty. The purpose is to test whether the observed representation/control dissociation is caused by broadcast scope or by the semantic direction itself.
